name: Duckweed
description: The fastest-reproducing flowering plant on Earth, doubling biomass every 24-48 hours through clonal budding. Smallest known angiosperm (Wolffia: 0.6mm) achieves maximal surface-to-volume ratio for nutrient uptake. Phytoremediation powerhouse that absorbs nitrogen, phosphorus, and heavy metals from water. Protein-rich biomass (up to 45% dry weight) makes it a living bioreactor.

core_attributes.pattern: exponential clonal reproduction, phytoremediation, nutrient hyperaccumulation

scope.definition: Biomass doubling rate of Lemna minor under optimal nutrient and light conditions — ratio of achieved doubling time (24-48h) to theoretical minimum for C3 aquatic photosynthesis.

evidence.source: Landolt & Kandeler (1987) 'The Family of Lemnaceae', Geobotanischen Instituts; Ziegler et al. (2015) duckweed bioremediation and growth studies.
cross_domain_examples: Lemna minor doubles biomass every 24-48h under optimal conditions — fastest flowering plant growth rate
protein content 25-45% dry weight — higher than soy, with comparable essential amino acid profile
microalgae (Spirulina): equivalent rapid doubling time for single-celled photosynthesizer — multi-cell analogue

scope.falsifiability: If Lemna minor growth rate under optimal conditions is statistically indistinguishable from other aquatic plants at equivalent biomass density, the exceptional growth rate is a size effect, not metabolic efficiency.
scope.measurement_limits: Doubling time is nutrient-concentration dependent — phosphorus is typically limiting in natural systems. Overcrowding causes light self-shading that reduces growth to 4-7 day doubling time.
